description: The plot titled “Hidden State Mean” illustrates the absolute mean values of hidden states across different layers in a neural network, comparing three conditions: “hidden state mean before gate,” “hidden state mean after gate,” and “hidden state mean of baseline.” The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to approximately 22 with linear spacing and integer tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled “Abs Mean,” ranges from 0 to 4.5 with linear scaling and major tick marks at intervals of 1. The blue dashed line representing “hidden state mean before gate” starts near 0 at layer 0, remains low (around 0.1–0.3) through layer 15, then rises sharply to approximately 2.6 at layer 20 and jumps to over 4.2 by layer 22. The orange dotted line for “hidden state mean after gate” stays near zero across all layers, with a slight upward trend visible after layer 15, reaching about 0.08 at layer 22. The green solid line for “hidden state mean of baseline” remains nearly flat and close to zero throughout, peaking slightly around layer 20 at approximately 0.05 before declining slightly. The legend indicates average values for each line: 0.71 for before gate, 0.05 for after gate, and 0.04 for baseline, reflecting the overall magnitude differences observed in the plot.
